key_highlights: ASX shed $90bn in a week amid rate-rise fears and oil price surge, signalling sharp risk-off rotation
AUD weakened materially as growth scare builds, pressuring import-heavy and foreign-revenue ASX names
Iron ore entering a 'bloodletting' phase, directly threatening BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX earnings trajectories
Oil price spike (price suppression failing) lifts fuel costs by ~30c/L, squeezing Qantas.AX, airline sector, and consumer discretionary
ANZ.AX post-3,500-job-cut restructuring plan faces execution risk; financials under structural pressure
Housing market correction deepens: no spring bounce at auctions, prices falling, first-home-buyer surge
Fed rate hike this week (hot US inflation) adds external rate pressure, complicating RBA path
Mining cap-raise wave (Canaccord-led) signals capital stress across junior/intermediate miners
BRICS 2026 summit and Chinese Arctic shipping route signal shifting trade/geopolitical dynamics for commodity exporters
AI sector caution: top tech execs call for slowdown; Anthropic-led concerns weigh on global tech sentiment

sectors.trend: Iron ore in active 'bloodletting'; gold underperforming ('schmould'); junior miners scrambling for cap raises via Canaccord-led dash. Commodity revenue headwinds across the board.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin compression; Sunstone Metals, Manuka Resources, PolarX (ASX runners) show relative strength but remain speculative. Cap-raise dilution risk elevated.

sectors.trend: ANZ.AX restructuring post-3,500 cuts signals industry-wide cost pressure; rate-rise fears compress net interest margin outlook; housing correction threatens mortgage book quality.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX, ANZ.AX face dual squeeze: tighter credit conditions from housing downturn vs. rate-driven NIM support. Private health insurance 'cash grab' (pensioner impact) adds regulatory overhang.

sectors.trend: Oil price surge (suppression failing) is a double-edged sword: positive for Santos.AX, WDS.AX revenue but inflationary pressure on RBA and consumer spending. Fuel +30c/L hits transport and consumer staples.
sectors.implications: Santos.AX, Woodside.AX benefit from oil spike but 'Australia sacrificed to preserve Santos' narrative raises political/regulatory risk. Qantas.AX and airlines face acute cost pressure.

sectors.trend: Housing correction, rising fuel costs, and business confidence erosion ('Australian businesses fear for their future') point to consumer spending contraction. First-home-buyer surge is a partial offset.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WOW.AX, CSG.AX face margin pressure from input costs; REITs (GPW.AX, SPG.AX) pressured by rate environment and occupancy concerns.

sectors.trend: Queensland hyper-scale data centre (quarter of state power) signals structural demand; AI slowdown calls from global tech leaders create near-term sentiment drag but long-term infrastructure buildout continues.
sectors.implications: ASX-listed data/infrastructure plays and CSL.AX (healthcare tech) benefit from capex cycles; global AI caution (NVDA, AMD) may spill over into ASX tech sentiment.

sectors.trend: Private health insurance cost-shifting to pensioners; unapproved peptide safety incident; bird flu in endangered species. Sector structurally resilient but policy risk rising.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, SGH.AX, HIC.AX face regulatory scrutiny on pricing; defensive characteristics intact amid broader market stress.

defensive_moves.rationale: AUD 'smashed' on growth scare; import-cost inflation will compress margins for foreign-revenue firms

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce REIT and rate-sensitive growth exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Rate-rise fears and housing correction create headwinds for property and long-duration equities

market_outlook.short_term: Bearish. $90bn weekly ASX loss, AUD weakness, oil-driven inflation, and Fed rate hike this week create a hostile near-term environment. Expect continued volatility in ^AXJO and ^AORD. Iron ore weakness and mining cap raises add sector-specific stress. RBA likely on hold or hawkish given oil-inflation passthrough. 1–3 month bias: further 5–8% downside risk in ^AXJO if Fed hikes and AUD breaks key support.
market_outlook.long_term: Cautiously constructive. Housing correction may stabilise within 6–12 months as first-home-buyer surge absorbs supply. Energy transition (Queensland data centres, wind farms) supports structural capex. ANZ restructuring and financial-sector cost discipline should improve ROE by 2027. Iron ore oversupply may correct, but diversified miners retain strategic value. Superannuation system reform debate could create policy tailwinds for listed funds. Key risk: prolonged commodity downturn combined with rate compression.
